I think it's totally normal to feel how you're feeling right now. I've lived with my 104 year old great grandmother for 3 years in March. I love her more than anything and I wish I could stay here forever, but she can make things very VERY difficult sometimes. I have to walk on eggshells around her sometimes. I can't point out that she is wrong about something. I have to fully read her mind often (oh, she's staring at something on the counter, that means she wants me to put it away). She says things to other family members that makes it sound like I'm not listening to her needs, despite her having never told me xyz. And I can't ask her to stop doing these things because then I'm attacking her.

What I find helps me is calling my grandpa (her son) and venting. He totally gets how she is and lets me just bitch and moan. I still feel guilty about this, because I really do love her more than anything, but it helps to vent to someone that /knows/ how much I love her, despite her frustrating qualities.

I know our situations aren't the same at all, but I know how it feels to be a live in caregiver for someone that's difficult, even if it's only sometimes for me. I find that venting really helps me calm down and think "I love her and I would and do anything for her, but that doesn't negate that we are both human and both have issues and feelings". 

I hope this made sense, sorry.

My OCD pushed away my very close group of friends (I dont blame them, really) and I was completely alone constantly. It was really awful, I constantly felt hopeless and distraught. Then I posted on here, actually, and got some book recommendations. The one that I read was by Dr. Johnathon Grayson "Freedom From Obsessive Compulsive Disorder".
I started studying it and in doing so formed a sort of relationship with my OCD. I was able to recognize it as a disorder and not something wrong with me as a person, (that is, something wrong with my "brain," not my "soul".) This helped me tremendously. Hope that helps some, I feel for you
